title: Walmart (WMT) Agrees To $7.8 Million Pennsylvania Child Labor Settlement

Walmart (WMT) Agrees To $7.8 Million Pennsylvania Child Labor Settlement
Sasha Jovanovic
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 8:12 AM MST 3 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart (NasdaqGS:WMT) agreed to pay a record $7.8 million child labor settlement in Pennsylvania following state investigations.

Pennsylvania authorities found widespread violations of the state's Child Labor Act across Walmart locations, according to the settlement announcement.

The agreement requires Walmart to adopt enhanced child labor compliance measures and includes higher future penalty provisions for any new violations.

The record child labor settlement reshapes the compliance backdrop for Walmart and informs how investors may frame ongoing labor scrutiny. We have also flagged 2 other big wins for Walmart.

For readers tracking labor risk and regulation across large employers, the next logical step is to scan related opportunities through 42 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks.

NasdaqGS:WMT 1-Year Stock Price Chart

Walmart operates one of the largest global retail and wholesale networks through physical stores, warehouse clubs, ecommerce sites, and mobile apps, so any shift in its labor compliance obligations can influence how investors evaluate workforce practices across large scale consumer retailers.

See how Walmart's balance sheet measures up.

How big is this Walmart penalty in context?

The US$7.8 million figure is large for a child labor case in Pennsylvania, yet it is small against Walmart's scale, with revenue previously reported in the hundreds of billions of dollars. The cash hit looks limited, though it flags that compliance missteps in frontline operations can still convert into direct costs and management time.

What could this mean for Walmart's broader operating and labor model?

The settlement followed audits that found an average of 65 child labor violations per store audit at the sampled locations, which points to process issues rather than a one off event. Walmart is already investing around US$6b into automation over several years. Tighter labor controls now sit alongside that push as another operational priority that needs ongoing spend and oversight.

What is the clearest indicator to watch from here?

The key tell is how future Pennsylvania compliance checks play out under the agreement, because any new violations trigger double penalties relative to typical fines. Investors tracking Walmart's risk profile can watch for references to labor investigations, fines or penalty accruals in upcoming quarterly reports through 2027 as an early signal of whether the new controls are holding.

Home Depot (HD) stock returned 19.5% between October 13 and November 11, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 2.3%. The worry for a holder is whether that rebound lasts. Management has already committed to one thing: in August 2026, it reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 guidance while flagging fuel, energy and tariff costs it had not planned for. Below are the events most likely to move Home Depot stock over the next six months.

Against the stock

Home Depot's November Report

Home Depot is expected to report its next quarterly results in November 2026, the first of these events to land. On its August 18, 2026 call, management said the third quarter had started with demand in line with the second, while warning of frozen housing conditions and large, unplanned cost pressure. The same quarter a year earlier brought in $41.4 billion of revenue, the base this report will be measured against. Management said sales to Pro customers rose on a comparable basis in the second quarter and outpaced sales to do-it-yourself shoppers. The measure to watch is comparable sales growth, which was 1.7% in the quarter ended August 2, 2026.

Costs Home Depot Did Not Plan For

Management is holding Home Depot's fiscal 2026 profit guide even though costs have risen beyond what it planned at the start of the year. In August 2026, management said rising fuel, energy and other product input costs would fully offset the tariff refunds it received in the second quarter, and that tariff changes in July added to that pressure. Management still guided to an operating margin, before adjustments, of about 12.4% to 12.6% for fiscal 2026, part of the full-year guidance it reaffirmed on the call. Gross margin is the measure to watch in the November 2026 report, and management expects the fourth-quarter rate to be about flat with a year earlier. The November report covers the third quarter, so it will not show that rate; a year earlier, the third-quarter gross margin was 33.4%.

title: Walmart (WMT) Earnings Expected to Grow: What to Know Ahead of Next Week's Release
detail:
Walmart (WMT) Earnings Expected to Grow: What to Know Ahead of Next Week's Release
Zacks Equity Research
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 7:00 AM MST 4 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The market expects Walmart (WMT) to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended October 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook is important in assessing the company's earnings picture, but a powerful factor that might influence its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on November 19, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call will mostly determine the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations, it's worth having a handicapping insight into the odds of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This world's largest retailer is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.64 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +3.2%.

Revenues are expected to be $186.52 billion, up 3.9% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.15% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for WMT
Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.
